Playbook.name: Windows — Browser Extension Install - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A browser extension file (.xpi in a Firefox profile Extensions path, or similar) was created outside the normal install flow. Triage question: is this a malicious/unwanted extension being sideloaded for persistence/data theft, or a normal user extension install?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Malicious browser extensions steal session cookies/credentials and provide persistence within the user's browsing.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Browser extension created
Signal.Details: .xpi/extension file written to a browser profile Extensions path.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the extension was written.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the browser-extension file is a malicious sideload or a normal user install.

Step.name: The extension file and the writing process
Step.Purpose: A .xpi written by a non-browser process, or to an unusual path, indicates sideloading vs a user-initiated install.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "11" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE file.path RLIKE "(?i).*(.*extensions.*.*.*.xpi|.*extensions.*.*.*.crx)" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, file.path, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A .xpi/.crx written by the browser itself during a user install is normal. Written by a script/installer/other process, or into another user's profile, indicates sideloading. Note the process and path.

Step.name: Process context
Step.Purpose: Reveal whether a non-browser process placed the extension.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A dropper/script running near the extension write supports a malicious sideload.

Node.Condition: An extension file placed by a non-browser process or into an unusual/other-user profile path.
Node.Result: True Positive (Malicious/Unwanted Extension Sideload - investigate, remove)

Node.Condition: A user installing an extension through the browser's normal flow.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-EXT-WRITE, INV-02-EXT-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm with the user if needed; close as benign_activity.
Remove the extension; inspect it for credential/cookie theft; open IR if malicious.
Check the browser for session/credential exposure.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An enterprise extension-deployment tool installing extensions.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
